summary: Explain how controlling current or voltage reveals different aspects of a cell's electrical behavior.
outcomes: Distinguish commanded and measured variables in current- and voltage-clamp traces.
Recognize series resistance, space-clamp and recording-mode limitations.
sequence: Compare two recordings of the same simulated membrane
Define current clamp and voltage clamp
Interpret input resistance and current-voltage curves
Introduce whole-cell, cell-attached and perforated-patch concepts
Compare model predictions with archived cellular data

visual.question: Why do the two clamp modes answer different questions?
visual.interaction: Switch a simulated membrane between controlled-current and controlled-voltage modes and add nonideal resistance.

practice.task: Estimate simple membrane properties from synthetic clamp traces.
practice.success: Tracks command/response units and identifies a deliberately nonideal recording case.
